title: The sheep and the shepherd: why Christ hides his divinity
english: the plan of salvation of the flesh. For as a sheep to slaughter I was led, and as a lamb before its shearer is silent (Isaiah 53:7). Since the devil lies in wait for me, wanting to seize my flesh as a sheep, but fearing the divinity as a shepherd he withdraws and flees, for this reason I hide my divinity as a shepherd and put forward my flesh as a sheep, so that he may take courage and approach, and approaching may seize it, and seizing my flesh as a sheep he may be destroyed by the two-edged sword of the Spirit. Stop, then, heretic, condemning me for fear and ignorance. For I am afraid so that I may show the assumption of the flesh to be no illusion. I say, 'My soul is troubled,' so that you may learn that I have not assumed a body without a soul, as the error of Apollinaris wants it. Do not, then, attach the passions of the flesh to the impassible Word. For I am God and man, heretic: God, as the miracles guarantee; man, as the sufferings testify. Since therefore I am God and man, tell me who it is who suffered. If God suffered, you have spoken blasphemy. But if the flesh suffered, why do you attach the passion to the one on whom you do not cast the fear? For when one suffers, another does not fear, and when a man is crucified, God is not troubled. And that the flesh suffered while the Word remained impassible, Isaiah is witness, who, seeing me bloodied in the Spirit, asked, 'Why are your garments red?' Your garments, he says, are red, and not you. For the body is wounded, but the Word of the divinity is not harmed. And Jacob the patriarch is witness, who says concerning me, 'He will wash his robe in wine and his wrap in the blood of the grape' (Genesis 49:11). What robe? The body. What blood? That which flowed from the side.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Christ is still speaking in his own defense, explaining to the heretics why he displayed fear and human weakness before his passion.

title: The heretic's dilemma: if the Father did not remove the cup, either he could not or he would not
english: But if you do not throw out my testimony, I testify about myself. For my testimony is true, even if you do not want it to be—the testimony I spoke to the Jews: “Why do you want to kill me, a man who has spoken the truth to you?” (John 8:40). He said “a man,” heretic—not God. So this man Jesus, killed by the Jews, is the one who fears. And do not confuse the Word with your ignorance. I fear for this reason: so that death may grapple with me as with a man, and be defeated as by God. But even in fearing, I do not entirely refuse the passion. For if I refused it, I would not have said, “Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass” (Matthew 26:39). For I knew that nothing is impossible for the Father. But if I asked for death to be carried away, and he did not carry it away, two absurdities arise. For if he did not carry it away because he was unable, or because he spared not and handed me over, then you are found, heretic, attaching fear to me and powerlessness to the Father. But when you say that I fear, you are pardoned because of the flesh; yet when you attribute powerlessness to the Father, you sin without excuse, saying that the power of God is weaker than death. And in another way you make me out to be stronger than the Father. Let me tell you how. For if I, while living in the flesh, raised Lazarus, Jairus’s daughter, and the widow’s son, and after dying in the flesh, again plundered more than five hundred dead from their tombs, but my Father—who had no experience of flesh or death—could not rescue me, his beloved Son, from dangers—as he himself says, “This is my beloved Son” (Matthew 3:17)—then see what you are getting into, heretic.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Christ continues speaking in his own defense, now turning the heretic's charge back on him: if the Father did not remove the cup, the heretic must accuse either the Son of fear or the Father of powerlessness.

title: Christ's voluntary death as deception of the devil
english: By not granting me equality willingly, you grant me the greater thing against your will. The one you think you are disparaging for weakness, you are actually declaring stronger than the Father. For I, without even being urged on, rescued the souls held down in Hades. “Lord,” it says, “you brought up my soul from Hades” (Psalm 30:3). But he, even when urged on, did not free my troubled soul from the evils hanging over it. But let it not be so! For neither was the Father sparing or powerless when he did not free me from the passion, nor did I, in refusing the passion, ask for the cup to pass by. If the passion were involuntary, then I truly feared. But if the death was self-chosen, then I only appeared to fear, so that by deceiving the devil I might set humanity free. The devil did not see this, and so he dragged me down, intending to swallow me, not knowing that he would have to vomit up even those he had already swallowed. For the moment I stood in Hades, I stripped his tombs and laid bare his graves. I laid them bare not by fighting openly, but by invisibly providing the resurrection. I was releasing no one, and yet all were being released. I was saying nothing, and yet freedom was being proclaimed. I was calling no one, and yet all were running together. For the moment I stood there as king, the tyrant was despised. I shone as light, and the darkness was dissolved. You could see every prisoner looking at freedom, every captive dancing at the resurrection—so much so that the dead themselves were marveling at me for the victory and mocking death for its defeat, saying: “Where, death, is your sting? Where, Hades, is your victory?” (Hosea 13:14). And so it is. For all that has been said, let us send up glory to Christ, the king of all, for to him belong glory, honor, and worship, with the undefiled Father and the all-holy Spirit, to the ages of ages. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Christ is still speaking in the first person, answering the heretics' charge that his fear proves the Father's powerlessness.
